title: Quick-pin modal + endpoint templates playground notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight working doc to capture wireframe notes, microcopy experiments, and a small backlog checklist for the Quick‑Pin modal plus a tiny library of endpoint creation templates. Goal is to produce a minimally invasive quick pin experience that reduces accidental version freezes and keeps rollout/rollback paths obvious for engineers creating endpoints.

Context and constraints (assumptions):
- Primary users: platform engineers and product ML engineers creating endpoints under time pressure.
- We want 2 entry points to pinning: (A) the Catalog model page quick pin CTA, (B) the Endpoint create flow where pin is optional.
- Pin semantics: "Pinned" = explicit version lock for an endpoint route. Should be reversible. Provide soft pin (preference) for non-blocking suggestions.
- Must surface fallback behavior: if pinned model variant is unavailable, fallback to: pinned-compatible variant -> default latest -> fail with clear remediation.

Wireframe notes (sketch -> interaction):
1) Quick‑Pin modal (compact):
   - Header: "Pin model version to this endpoint" (smaller, single line)
   - Subhead: "Choose a specific model version to ensure consistent outputs. You can change this later."
   - Left column: small model card (name, architecture, quantization, last tested: 2025-02-01)
   - Center: dropdown of versions with radio list showing stability badge (recommended/experimental) and token cost delta per 1k tokens.
   - Right column: two small toggles: "Enable automatic fallback to compatible variant" (default on), "Deprioritize auto-update for minor patches" (default off)
   - Primary CTA: "Pin version" (strong, blue) Secondary: "Cancel".
   - Danger/confirm: if user picks an old version, show inline note: "This version is older — pinned endpoints remain on this exact version until unpinned. Confirm" with checkbox: "I understand" for versions >180 days old.

2) Inline nav within Endpoint Create flow:
   - Small chip under model selector: "Pin a version" -> opens the same compact modal.
   - If user does not pin, system shows tooltip: "Using latest compatible by default — performance/cost may change."

Microcopy experiments (variants included for A/B tests):
- Modal title variations: ["Pin model version to this endpoint", "Lock model version", "Fix model version (safe)" ]
- CTA primary: ["Pin version", "Lock and continue", "Set version"]
- Fallback toggle label: ["Enable automatic fallback", "Allow fallback to other variants", "Auto‑fallback (recommended)"]
- Old-version warning: ["This version is older and may lack security/bug fixes.", "Older version — pinning prevents automatic upgrades."]
- Success toast: ["Version pinned. You can unpin from endpoint settings.", "Pinned — endpoint locked to vX.XX. Unpin any time."]

Error states and edge cases:
- If pinned version is not available in selected region: modal shows amber badge: "Not currently available in us-west1. Select a different version or enable fallback."
- If pin would exceed SLA tier (e.g., reserved GPU mismatch): show inline help: "This version needs GPU X. Upgrade Dedicated tier or choose a CPU/quantized variant."
- Concurrent edits: if two users attempt to pin different versions simultaneously, use optimistic concurrency: show conflict banner in modal: "Another user changed the pin. Review the current selection."

Acceptance criteria (small, testable):
- Users can access the Quick‑Pin modal from Catalog and Endpoint Create.
- Pin action writes a pin record visible in endpoint config API and console UX within 5s.
- Unpin action is available from endpoint settings and requires confirmation for production routes.
- When fallback is ON and pinned version offline, endpoint serves compatible fallback variant without error and logs the substitution.

Backlog grooming items (rough sizes):
- PROJ-1201: Implement compact Quick‑Pin modal UI (3 days frontend) - owner: Evan Cho.
- PROJ-1202: API: pin/unpin endpoints + audit trail (4 days backend) - owner: Diego Alvarez.
- PROJ-1203: Add version availability checks by region (2 days infra) - owner: Marissa Klein.
- PROJ-1204: Add microcopy A/B test scaffold for modal CTAs (1 day) - owner: Priya Raman.
- PROJ-1205: Rollout policy: add toggle for auto‑fallback default (2 days product + QA) - owner: product.

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Default behavior for newly created endpoints: pin by default for Dedicated tier? (pros: predictability; cons: friction)
- Should we surface token-cost deltas prominently in the modal or keep it subtle? (ask finance for threshold)
- What is the audit log retention policy for pin changes? 90 days or 365? (security to weigh in)

Playbook copy snippets to reuse across console (final candidates):
- Tooltip for "Pin a version": "Lock this endpoint to a specific model version so outputs stay stable. You can change or unpin later."
- Button (primary): "Pin version"
- Inline confirmation: "Pinning will prevent automatic updates — continue?"

Next steps (short):
- Quick prototype in Figma using the compact modal, wire size for mobile (narrow) and desktop. (Evan)
- Backend API sketch and data model for pin records + audit fields (Diego)
- Bring to product design review Thurs 03/06 — confirm defaults and danger copy (Priya + Marissa)

Notes to reviewers: this doc intentionally leaves several microcopy variants to AB test early. Keep the modal compact: core hypothesis is that shorter flows with a clear fallback toggle reduce accidental pins and support safe rollouts.

History / iteration notes: created as spin-off from larger Catalog UX refresh doc; this focuses on the minimum invokable surface for pinning and small endpoint templates for fast onboarding.
